questions.prompt: Two responses sit beside the same full sink: Mila waits for her partner to notice; Holly says, "I need us to alternate dishes tonight." Which response fits direct intimacy boundaries?
choices: Mind-Reading Test: Mila waits so love can prove it noticed the sink.
Clear Terms: Holly names the dishes and asks for a shared plan.
Care Verdict: Mila treats the sink as proof her partner values her less.

questions.prompt: A log of 5 arguments shows each began with one chore and ended with money, sex, and holiday plans. What should Beau infer first?
choices: One-Subject Repair: Beau should keep the next talk on the first chore.
Archive Sweep: Beau should schedule one talk for several old hurts.
Intensity Fix: Beau should raise the stakes so the pattern feels serious.

questions.prompt: Ivy says no to sex after a long shift. One reply bargains for reassurance; another accepts tonight's no. Which reply respects the boundary?
choices: Reassurance Bargain: Her partner asks Ivy to prove she still wants the relationship.
History Claim: Her partner points to past closeness as tonight's reason.
Consent Respect: Her partner accepts tonight's no and drops the pressure.

questions.prompt: Janelle's chore notes show 6 straight nights of pans done by her, plus 3 hints her partner missed. What is the cleanest boundary move?
choices: Silent Scorekeeping: Janelle keeps counting until the imbalance is obvious.
Shared Terms: Janelle asks for a named split before the next dinner.
Moral Guessing: Janelle waits for her partner to discover the right chore.

questions.prompt: Georges wants 20 quiet minutes after work. Two responses are available: apologize for needing space, or state the limit and return at a set time. Which one respects romance and privacy?
choices: Timed Privacy: Georges takes 20 quiet minutes and returns when promised.
Access Proof: Georges treats constant availability as the price of love.
Guilt Payment: Georges apologizes until his partner stops feeling uneasy.

questions.prompt: A text thread shows three jokes after Mila already said touch is off tonight. Which follow-through matches the boundary?
choices: Mood Management: Mila softens the no until the jokes fade by themselves.
Debt Logic: Mila weighs whether past closeness makes the jokes fair.
Body-Limit Follow-Through: Mila ends the thread and revisits closeness tomorrow.

questions.prompt: At a highway rest stop counter, Georges hears himself bargain after his partner said no to motel sex, and the receipt is still in his hand. What is the first repair move?
choices: Intent Defense: Georges explains he only wanted closeness during the trip.
Timing Debate: Georges asks whether a shorter pause would feel acceptable.
Pressure Repair: Georges names the push, stops asking, and respects the no.

questions.prompt: Two partners state limits: Holly will not wash pans nightly; Beau needs Sunday talk to stay on one subject. What should each person allow from the other?
choices: Winner Frame: Each treats the first clear limit as the final relationship rule.
Reciprocal Clarity: Each hears the limit and answers with their own truth.
Approval Chase: Each keeps explaining until the other person likes the limit.

questions.prompt: After an argument, Ivy's notes list one apology, one rent-date fix, and three old grievances she wants to add. Which next step aims at repair?
choices: Repair Focus: Ivy handles the rent-date fix before opening another topic.
History Trial: Ivy adds the old grievances so the repair feels complete.
Peacekeeping Silence: Ivy drops the rent issue to avoid a second talk.
